mock.jd.positioning: This {{role}} role centers on shipping reliable, measurable AI features end to end.
mock.jd.core1: Own the {{role}} roadmap and delivery from problem to production.
mock.jd.core2: Define quality and evaluation metrics for AI outputs.
mock.jd.core3: Partner with engineering on retrieval, prompts and agent workflows.
mock.jd.must2: Strong grasp of evaluation, quality and failure modes.
mock.jd.must3: Ability to balance latency, cost and reliability.
mock.jd.nice1: Experience with RAG and agent architectures.
mock.jd.nice2: Familiarity with experimentation and A/B testing.
mock.jd.implicit1: Comfort operating with ambiguity and fast iteration.
mock.jd.implicit2: Clear written communication for cross-functional alignment.
mock.resume.sell1: Shipped an AI feature to production with measurable impact.
mock.resume.sell2: Built an evaluation harness combining human and automated scoring.
mock.resume.match2: Worked closely with ML engineers on iteration.
mock.resume.gap1: Limited evidence of cost / latency optimization at scale.
mock.resume.gap2: Few details on stakeholder and roadmap ownership.
mock.resume.probe1: How exactly was answer quality measured?
mock.resume.probe2: What tradeoffs were made on cost vs. quality?
mock.resume.ev1: Prepare concrete metrics for your shipped AI feature.
mock.resume.ev2: Have a clear story on an eval you designed.
mock.match.strong1: Production AI experience aligns with the core requirement.
mock.match.strong2: Evaluation mindset matches the role's quality focus.
mock.match.weak1: Cost / latency optimization needs stronger evidence.
mock.match.weak2: Scale and reliability stories could be sharper.
mock.match.risk1: Be ready to quantify impact; vague metrics are a red flag.
mock.match.advice1: Prepare two STAR stories tied to measurable AI outcomes.
mock.match.advice2: Rehearse a crisp explanation of an eval you built.
mock.plan.s1f: Background and motivation for the role.
mock.plan.s2f: Deep-dive on AI product / technical judgment.
mock.iv.q1: To start, walk me through a recent AI project you owned and why it mattered.
mock.iv.q2: How did you measure the quality of your AI feature? Be specific about metrics.
mock.iv.q3: Tell me about a time the model behaved unexpectedly. How did you diagnose and fix it?
mock.iv.q4: Imagine latency doubled in production but quality improved. How would you decide what to ship?
mock.iv.q5: What questions do you have for us, and what would make this role a strong fit for you?
mock.fb.overview: A solid interview overall. You showed real AI product experience and an evaluation mindset, but several answers needed sharper metrics and clearer tradeoff reasoning to be fully convincing.
mock.fb.strength1: Clear, structured storytelling with concrete project context.
mock.fb.strength2: Good instinct for measuring AI output quality.
mock.fb.weak1: Metrics were sometimes vague; quantify outcomes more.
mock.fb.weak2: Tradeoff reasoning (cost vs. quality) could be more explicit.
mock.fb.risk1: The latency-vs-quality answer lacked a clear decision framework.
mock.fb.prob1: The answer stayed high-level without concrete numbers.
mock.fb.prob2: Missing a clear structure (situation, action, result).
mock.fb.dir1: Lead with the metric and the impact, then explain how.
mock.fb.dir2: Name the tradeoff explicitly and your decision criteria.
mock.fb.optAnswer: In my last role I owned a support assistant using RAG. I defined answer quality as a blend of human-rated helpfulness and automated factuality checks, and set a target of 90% helpful responses. We hit 92% while cutting cost per query 35% by caching retrieval and right-sizing the model. The key tradeoff was latency vs. quality: I shipped the faster model once eval scores stayed within 2 points of the larger one.
mock.fb.practice1: Write down three measurable outcomes from past AI work.
mock.fb.practice2: Practice a 90-second STAR answer for your strongest project.
mock.fb.practice3: Prepare a decision framework for cost vs. quality tradeoffs.
mock.iv.q1.intent: Assess ownership and ability to frame impact.
mock.iv.q2.intent: Probe depth on evaluation and metrics thinking.
mock.iv.q3.intent: Test debugging instinct and failure-mode awareness.
mock.iv.q4.intent: Evaluate tradeoff reasoning under real constraints.
mock.fb.improve1: Quantify every outcome — lead with the metric, then the method.
mock.fb.improve2: Name tradeoffs explicitly and state your decision criteria.
mock.fb.improve3: Tighten answer structure using situation, action, result.
mock.fb.next1: Run a stress-style product interview to practice ambiguity.
mock.fb.next2: Drill metric-driven storytelling for your top two projects.
mock.fb.followup1: Could you share the exact numbers behind that result?
mock.fb.followup2: What would you have done if quality had dropped instead?
mock.hint.low: Too brief — add specifics and a concrete result.
mock.hint.mid: Solid — consider adding a metric or tradeoff.
